classification.difficultyReason: Construct valid nets by identifying matching end faces and arranging side rectangles; the triangular prism requires matching three different triangle edges to rectangle widths.

content.prompt: Sketch a net for each of these shapes.

spec.description: Upright square prism with front, left and top faces visible. External arrows label both perpendicular base edges 2 cm and the height 7 cm.
spec.mathematics: Explicit front, left and top face polygons. Hidden back and bottom edges are omitted, as in the source; the visible silhouette is solid.
spec.answerVisibility: Both 2 cm labels and the 7 cm label are permanent givens.

answer.short: Four $7\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$ rectangles and two $2\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$ squares.
answer.worked: Join four $7\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$ rectangles in a strip. Attach one $2\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$ square at each end of the prism.

spec.description: One valid net: four tall rectangles in a horizontal strip and two squares attached above and below the second rectangle.
spec.mathematics: Four 2 by 7 rectangles and two 2 by 2 squares; solid cut edges and dashed fold edges.

spec.description: Triangular prism extending upward-right from its near triangular end. The near triangle has bottom edge 3 cm, left edge 4 cm and sloping edge 5 cm. The right receding edge is labelled 6 cm.
spec.mathematics: Congruent 3–4–5 triangular ends separated by a prism length of 6 cm. Explicit face polygons define the near triangle and lateral faces. Only source-visible edges are drawn; no right-angle marker is added.
spec.answerVisibility: All four measurements are permanent givens.

answer.short: Two $3$–$4$–$5\text{ cm}$ triangles and rectangles measuring $6\text{ cm}\times3\text{ cm}$, $6\text{ cm}\times4\text{ cm}$ and $6\text{ cm}\times5\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked: Join the three rectangles in a strip along their $6\text{ cm}$ edges. Attach two congruent $3$–$4$–$5\text{ cm}$ triangles to matching edges at opposite ends of the prism.

spec.description: One valid triangular-prism net with rectangles of widths 3, 4 and 5 cm and common length 6 cm. Congruent triangular ends attach to the 3 cm edges of the first rectangle.
spec.mathematics: Triangle legs are 3 and 4 cm and hypotenuse is 5 cm; 3 squared plus 4 squared equals 5 squared. Solid cut edges and dashed folds preserve all five faces.
